title: Grateful Dead Live at P.N.E. Coliseum on 1973-06-22
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Samplitude Professional v9.12 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat (44.1k) D

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a laid‑back yet soaring 1973 Vancouver show with standout Playin’ in the Band and an epic He's Gone > Truckin' > The Other One sequence.
ai_review.review: This recording delivers crystal‑clear, expertly mixed soundboard audio that lets every instrument shine—from Jerry’s silky guitar tones to Keith’s lush piano. The performance is a relaxed, exploratory marathon of classic ’73 material, highlighted by a one‑of‑a‑kind Playin’ In The Band, an unforgettable Bird Song, and the powerhouse He’s Gone > Truckin' > The Other One stretch with a killer bass solo.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly praise both the musical performance and the soundboard quality; weighted rating (70% show, 30% recording) yields a near‑exceptional score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix with superb EQ; Charlie Miller’s mastering brings out each instrument. Minor complaints about the Bird Song edit and occasional Bertha hiss, but overall the audio is clean and highly listenable.

standout_songs: He's Gone > Truckin' > The Other One
show_quality.setlist_flow: A relaxed first set that gradually builds into a high‑energy second half, with seamless transitions and extended jams that keep the momentum alive throughout the long show.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeated praise for his silky guitar tone, watery solo work, and overall stellar lead playing.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass solo in the Truckin' jam described as "gold"; frequent "bombs" and teasing of future songs noted, plus strong tonal presence throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Rhythm guitar praised for solid support and nice tone, especially during Black Peter and other mid‑set numbers.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's piano/electric piano highlighted as sensitive, prominent, and a key driver of the jazzy, spacey feel; his work on Bird Song and transitions noted.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill (drummer) commended for tight, jazz‑inflected playing that underpins the extended jams.
